From highest to lowest, U.S. law runs: the Constitution; federal treaties and statutes, which are generally coequal (the later-in-time one controls when they conflict); federal regulations; then state constitutions, state statutes, state regulations, and local ordinances. Under the Supremacy Clause (Article VI), valid federal law overrides conflicting state law, and Supreme Court rulings on federal law bind lower courts nationwide. The treaty-statute ranking and the role of common law vary by context.
